description: Reading documents: format selection, the data model, static reading, limits, the dotenv grammar and substitution. Input is 'text' (UTF-8) or 'base64'; 'format' is 'aos' (overlay.cfg rules), 'dotenv', 'env-script' (an env script's output, whose data maps a variable to a string, or to null to unset it), or 'catalog' (a catalog document, whose file 'name' selects its format by extension). A dotenv case may give 'env' (the environment before the file; absent, empty), 'os' ('windows' compares names without regard to ASCII case; absent, another OS) and 'secret_variables' (the names in 'env' whose value came from a secret reference); its data is what each line sets, substituted against the environment the earlier lines left. 'expect' is the data, or an error class (a list when either class is right); with both 'data' and 'error', either outcome is right.

priority: 420
requires: [engineering]

  MODE: read-only

cases.description: A byte-order mark and CRLF line ends.
Quotes are removed only in matching pairs.
A line that is not NAME=VALUE.
A name given twice.
Names that differ only in ASCII case are one variable on Windows.
A name must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*.

cases.description: Only the outermost matching pair is removed; inner quotes stay.
'export=1' sets a variable named export.
'export' alone is not NAME=VALUE.
A line starting with '=' has no name.
A quote does not continue onto the next line.
${NAME} is the variable's value, anywhere in a value.
Only the braced form is a placeholder: $NAME, a lone $ and $5 are characters.
$$ is one $, so $${NAME} is the text ${NAME}.
Command substitution and arithmetic are characters.
An expression AOS does not define is text: its $ is itself and reading goes on after it.
Reading goes on inside an unknown expression, so a placeholder there is substituted.
An undefined name is an error.
The length of an undefined name is an error.
A slice of an undefined name is an error.
A replacement in an undefined name is an error.
A trim of an undefined name is an error.
A case change of an undefined name is an error.
${NAME-} and ${NAME:-} give an empty value where the name is unset: the author's way to allow it.
'-' replaces an unset name; ':-' an unset or empty one; '=' and ':=' read the same and assign nothing.
${NAME=word} sets nothing: the name is still unset on the next line.
'+' gives the word for a set name; ':+' for a set and non-empty one; otherwise empty.
A default's or alternate's word is substituted itself.
A word is substituted only when it is used, so an undefined name in an unused word is no error.
Quotes in a word are characters.
${#NAME} is the number of Unicode code points, in decimal.
${NAME:offset} and ${NAME:offset:length}; a negative offset needs a space or parentheses, since ':-' is a default; a negative length counts from the end.
Not a slice, so text: an empty length, a space inside '- 5', a non-ASCII digit.
Offsets count Unicode code points, not bytes or UTF-16 units.
'/' replaces the first match, '//' every match, '/#' a match at the start, '/%' at the end; no text deletes; an empty pattern changes nothing.
Patterns are globs, matched longest first: '*', '?', bracket expressions with ranges and '!' or '^' negation, a ']' first in the brackets, '\' for the next character.
A '/' in the pattern is written '\/'; the replacement is characters, a backslash or a placeholder included.
On an empty value '/' and '//' replace nothing, while '/#' and '/%' replace the empty match.
A '[' with no ']' after the character that follows it is itself.
A range whose end is before its start is an error.
Brackets holding only the negation mark are an error.
Also when a later bracket expression follows: '[!]' never joins it.
'#' removes the shortest matching prefix, '##' the longest; '%' the shortest matching suffix, '%%' the longest.
'^' upper-cases the first character, '^^' all; ',' and ',,' lower-case; Unicode full case mapping.
A value in single quotes is literal; double quotes, or none, are substituted.
Each line sees the lines before it.
A variable refers to its own earlier value.
A variable set on a later line is not set yet: undefined, an error.
A later line has not run yet, so the name still has its earlier value.
A value is inserted as it is: placeholders in it are not substituted again, so nothing can loop.
Off Windows a name matches only in its own case.
On Windows a name matches without regard to ASCII case.
A variable whose value came from a secret reference is never read by a placeholder.
In any form: not its length ...
... nor whether it is set.
A secret named in a word that is not used is not read.
Once a later line sets the variable, it no longer holds the secret.
One JSON object per line, applied in order: blank lines skipped, CRLF accepted, null unsets.
The whole output as one object over several lines, as json.dumps(x, indent=2) prints it.
No output, or only blank lines, sets nothing.
Two pretty-printed objects are neither one object nor one object per line.
Each object is a JSON object.
A value is a string or null.
A reserved variable is refused.
A key given twice in one object is refused, pretty-printed too.
Any other output fails.
